function getParameterByName(name, url) {
		if(url == null){
		  url = window.location.href;
		}
	    name = name.replace(/[\[\]]/g, '\\$&');
	    var regex = new RegExp('[?&]' + name + '(=([^&#]*)|&|#|$)'),
		results = regex.exec(url);
	    if (!results) return null;
	    if (!results[2]) return '';
	    return decodeURIComponent(results[2].replace(/\+/g, ' '));
	}

    function addStyle(parent, id, def) {

        return;

            return;

 * String.prototype.replaceAll() polyfill

	String.prototype.replaceAll = function(str, newStr){
		// If a regex pattern
		if (Object.prototype.toString.call(str).toLowerCase() === '[object regexp]') {
			return this.replace(str, newStr);
		}
		// If a string
		return this.replace(new RegExp(str, 'g'), newStr);

	function getCookie(cname) {
	 	var name = cname + "=";
  		var decodedCookie = decodeURIComponent(document.cookie);
		var ca = decodedCookie.split(';');
  		for(var i = 0; i <ca.length; i++) {
    			var c = ca[i];
    			while (c.charAt(0) == ' ') {
     				 c = c.substring(1);
    			}
    			if (c.indexOf(name) == 0) {
    				 return c.substring(name.length, c.length);
    			}
  		}
  		return "";
	}

	var referer = "";//sessionStorage.container;
	var pcontainer = sessionStorage.getItem("container");

function callMainSitePrismaNavHTML(){
    
    var referrer_domain = 'https://www.paloaltonetworks.com';
    sessionStorage.setItem("domain",referrer_domain);
    if(referer == 'Prisma'){

        }
    if(referer == 'CloudCortex'){

        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/cortexcloudsearch";	
    }

        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/cortexsearch";	
    }
    if(referer == 'Sase'){
        //var menu_url = referrer_domain+'/_jcr_content/globals/cleanHeaderSase.saseRenderer.html';
        var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/unit-nav-renderer.php?type=sase&domain=en';
        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/sasesearch";
    }
    if(referer == 'Unit'){
        var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/unit-nav-renderer.php?type=unit42&domain=en';
        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/content/pan/en_US/search/unit42search";
		    }
    if(referer == 'Ngfw'){

        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/ngfwcdsssearch";

        //var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/ngfw-cdss-nav-renderer.php';
        var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/unit-nav-renderer.php?type=idira&domain=en';

    }
    httpGet(menu_url,'menu_html');

}
function addStyle(styles) {            
    /* Create style document */
    var css = document.createElement('style');
    css.type = 'text/css';

    if (css.styleSheet) 
        css.styleSheet.cssText = styles;
    else 
        css.appendChild(document.createTextNode(styles));

    /* Append style to the tag name */
    document.getElementsByTagName("head")[0].appendChild(css);
}
function httpGet(theUrl,req_type) {
    if (window.XMLHttpRequest) { // code for IE7+, Firefox, Chrome, Opera, Safari
        xmlhttp=new XMLHttpRequest();
    } else {// code for IE6, IE5
        xmlhttp=new ActiveXObject("Microsoft.XMLHTTP");
    }
    xmlhttp.onreadystatechange=function()
    {
        if (xmlhttp.readyState==4 && xmlhttp.status==200)
        {
            if(req_type == 'menu_html'){
            var nav_text = xmlhttp.responseText.replaceAll('https://static.cloud.coveo.com/searchui/v2.9159/js/CoveoJsSearch.Lazy.min.js', '');
            nav_text = nav_text.replaceAll('src="/', 'src="'+maindomain_lang+'/');
            nav_text = nav_text.replaceAll("src='/", "src='"+maindomain_lang+"/");
            nav_text = nav_text.replaceAll("'/content", "'"+maindomain_lang+"/content");
                        
            document.getElementById("PAN_2021_NAV_ASYNC").innerHTML = nav_text.replaceAll('href="/', 'href="'+maindomain_lang+'/');

            var lozad_back = document.getElementsByClassName('lozad-background');
            Array.prototype.forEach.call(lozad_back, function(el) {
            // Do stuff here
            var el_back_img_path = el.getAttribute('data-background-image');
            var first_pos = el_back_img_path.indexOf("'");
            var last_pos = el_back_img_path.indexOf("'",first_pos+1);
            el_back_img_path = el_back_img_path.substring(first_pos+1,last_pos);
            let result = el_back_img_path.includes(main_site_url);
            if(result == false){
                el.setAttribute("data-background-image",main_site_url+el_back_img_path);
            }
            else{
                el.setAttribute("data-background-image",el_back_img_path);
            }
            });
            const observer_lozad = lozad('.lozad, .lozad-background'); // lazy loads elements with default selector as '.lozad'
            observer_lozad.observe();
            }
            if(req_type == 'head_inline_css'){
            addStyle(xmlhttp.responseText);
            }
        }
    }
    xmlhttp.open("GET", theUrl, true );
    xmlhttp.send();    
}    
    
if(referer == 'Prisma' || referer == 'CloudCortex' || referer == 'Cortex' || referer == 'Sase' || referer == 'Unit' || referer == 'Ngfw' || referer == 'Idira'){

    }
    else if(referer == 'Sase'){
        article.dataset.type = 'sase';

    else if(referer == 'Unit'){
        article.dataset.type = 'unit';
    }
    else if(referer == 'Ngfw'){
        article.dataset.type = 'ngfw';
    }
    else if(referer == 'Idira'){
        article.dataset.type = 'idira';
    }
    //set class to default

        $('#PAN_2021_NAV_ASYNC').removeClass('default').addClass('defaultRedesigned');

}

    <section class="section blog-contents"> 
      <div class="pa blog-editor">
        <div class="l-container">
          <div class="be__wrapper">
            <div class="be__contents">
              <div class="be__contents-wrapper">
                <h2><a id="post-183287-_4lt92rr5muov"></a>Executive Summary</h2>
<p>In April 2026, Unit 42 researchers identified a financially motivated campaign delivering Vidar stealer and the XMRig cryptocurrency miner to consumer and small- and medium-sized business victims worldwide.</p>
<p>Attackers lure victims via malvertising to pages for downloading files that impersonate cracked versions of copyright-protected software. Upon execution, the loader drops and runs both Vidar stealer and XMRig. Vidar stealer targets information like browser credentials, cookies and crypto wallets. XMRig mines Monero cryptocurrency.</p>
<p>We assess the operator of the campaign to be a Vidar stealer malware-as-a-service (MaaS) affiliate involved in operations targeting victims in the U.S. and European Union. This article provides a technical analysis of the campaign.</p>
<p>Palo Alto Networks customers are better protected from the threats discussed above through the following products and services:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/cortex/cortex-xdr?_gl=1*13pmp8e*_ga*NzQyNjM2NzkuMTY2NjY3OTczNw..*_ga_KS2MELEEFC*MTY2OTczNjA2MS4zMS4wLjE2Njk3MzYwNjEuNjAuMC4w" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Cortex XDR</a> and <a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/resources/datasheets/cortex-xsiam-aag" target="_blank" rel="noopener">XSIAM</a></li>
<li><a href="https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/advanced-threat-prevention/administration" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Advanced WildFire</a></li>
<li><a href="https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/advanced-url-filtering" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Advanced URL Filtering</a> and <a href="https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/dns-security" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Advanced DNS Security</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/sase/prisma-browser" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Prisma Browser</a></li>
</ul>
<p>If you think you might have been compromised or have an urgent matter, contact the <a href="https://start.paloaltonetworks.com/contact-unit42.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Unit 42 Incident Response team</a>.</p>
<table style="width: 100%;">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="width: 35%;"><b>Related Unit 42 Topics</b></td>
<td style="width: 100%;"><strong><a href="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tag/vidar-stealer/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Vidar Stealer</a>, <a href="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tag/Malware/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Malware</a>, <a href="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tag/cryptocurrency/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Cryptocurrency</a>, <a href="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tag/xmrig/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">XMRig</a></strong></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_vezf8g2kzzq1"></a>Attack Timeline</h2>
<p>Since its emergence, attackers have used Vidar stealer in multiple large-scale campaigns. We identified a notable spike in activity from mid-late April 2026, primarily targeting organizations in the U.S. and the EU.</p>
<p>Figure 1 illustrates the timeline of the April 2026 campaign, which shows the number of Vidar stealer samples discovered each day.</p>
<figure id="attachment_183359" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-183359" style="width: 709px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-183359 size-medium lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Vidar-Samples-709x440.png" alt="A bar chart showing Vidar Stealer sample campaign counts from April 15 to May 5, 2026. Peaks around April 21 and 22 with counts reaching 31 and 33. Other days show lower counts. Dates on the x-axis and sample counts on the y-axis." width="709" height="440" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Vidar-Samples-709x440.png 709w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Vidar-Samples.png 711w" sizes="(max-width: 709px) 100vw, 709px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-183359" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 1. April 2026 campaign.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Our investigation of this activity led to the discovery of loader binaries distributing both Vidar stealer and XMRig.</p>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_bv17a2it9p9k"></a>Initial Access: Malvertising via Fake Software Cracks</h2>
<p>This group behind this campaign distributes loader binaries through <a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/2015/01/malvertising-dawn-new-attack-era/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">malvertising</a>, targeting victims who search for pirated or cracked versions of copyright-protected software. The filenames used in this campaign mimic cracked versions of popular copyright-protected programs as well as generic installers.</p>
<p>The campaign delivers the malware in password-protected archives with a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">.bin</span> extension in the filenames. This appears to be a deliberate choice to bypass email gateway scanning and to prevent automated sandbox detonation without the password.</p>
<p>We initially discovered 43 of these loader binaries that deliver Vidar stealer and XMRig. Upon extraction and execution, the loader binary is signed with a certificate (subject <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">CN=justwatch[.]com</span>), creating a false sense of legitimacy before any malicious activity begins.</p>
<p>Our analysis of these loader samples indicates they use the Factory-v3 framework.</p>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_oi23ki7dx47e"></a>Factory-v3/UpdateFactory Builder</h2>
<p>Factory-v3 has been <a href="https://stevevanasche.me/post/invoke-clickfix-analysis#factory-v3-builder-attribution" target="_blank" rel="noopener">described as a MaaS builder</a> used for different families of stealer malware. All 43 samples we discovered from this campaign contain embedded Go build metadata identifying the Factory-v3 framework.</p>
<p>The Factory-v3 builder's internal name of <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">UpdateFactor</span> is revealed in a developer/build machine path shown in the programming database (PDB) strings of the loader DLL files:</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\UpdateFactory\compiler\1.25.9\go\src\runtime\cgo</span></p>
<p>Figure 2 shows a diagram of information from the build machine metadata.</p>
<figure id="attachment_183299" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-183299" style="width: 786px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-183299 size-medium lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-674652-183287-2-786x429.png" alt="A flowchart titled &quot;Build Metadata&quot; with two branches: &quot;EXE Variants&quot; and &quot;DLL Variants.&quot; Both branches lead to &quot;Factory-v3 builder.&quot; " width="786" height="429" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-674652-183287-2-786x429.png 786w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-674652-183287-2-1283x700.png 1283w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-674652-183287-2-768x419.png 768w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-674652-183287-2-1536x838.png 1536w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-674652-183287-2.png 2048w" sizes="(max-width: 786px) 100vw, 786px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-183299" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 2. Information from the build machine path.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The builder generates a unique binary per build. For example, we observed 27 unique build UUIDs across 43 samples, defeating hash-based detection. The builder uses <a href="https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#:~:text=tracker%20for%20details.-,go1.25.9,-(released%202026%2D04" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Go version 1.25.9</a>, a custom pre-release of tools for the Go programming language.</p>
<p>Anti-forensic measures are consistent across all samples:</p>
<ul>
<li>The PE <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">TimeDateStamp</span> is zeroed</li>
<li>No PE version info is present</li>
<li>DLL imports are reduced to <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">kernel32.dll</span> only</li>
<li>User-defined type names are obfuscated to a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">V######</span> pattern</li>
</ul>
<p>The same builder, toolchain and Authenticode certificate infrastructure underpin a concurrent Lumma stealer campaign. This indicates Factory-v3 is used as a service for multiple stealer affiliates.</p>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_t20dntwjcqgt"></a>Rogue Authenticode Certificate</h2>
<p>All 43 loader samples carry an Authenticode signature fabricated to impersonate JustWatch GmbH, a legitimate German streaming guide service. JustWatch has not been compromised. The certificate is entirely fabricated using a self-signed root certificate authority (CA) that is not present in any public trust store, as shown below in Figure 3.</p>
<figure id="attachment_183310" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-183310" style="width: 703px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-183310 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-677576-183287-3.png" alt="A screenshot of a roge certificate information displaying details such as the subject and issuer. The serial number is listed. It shows a 4096-bit RSA key with extended key usage for code signing and TLS. The certificate includes a beginning and end validation date. " width="703" height="149" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-183310" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 3. Rogue certificate information.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Because the certificate is not chained to a Microsoft-trusted root, Windows SmartScreen and Authenticode validation will flag the binary as untrusted. However, the visual presence of a recognizable brand name in the signature dialog is sufficient to deceive many victims into proceeding.</p>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_kvzqnxrujltl"></a>Sample Clusters</h2>
<p>The 43 loader samples fall into four clusters, as Table 1 below shows.</p>
<table style="width: 98.8271%;">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="width: 10.6367%; text-align: center;"><strong>Cluster</strong></td>
<td style="width: 17.5097%; text-align: center;"><strong>CPU Architecture</strong></td>
<td style="width: 13.6799%; text-align: center;"><strong>File Type</strong></td>
<td style="width: 19.8675%; text-align: center;"><strong>Frequency Count</strong></td>
<td style="width: 89.4252%; text-align: center;"><strong>Role</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 10.6367%; text-align: center;">A</td>
<td style="width: 17.5097%; text-align: center;">x64</td>
<td style="width: 13.6799%;">EXE</td>
<td style="width: 19.8675%; text-align: center;">26</td>
<td style="width: 89.4252%;">Go loader (file-inflated EXE)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 10.6367%; text-align: center;">B</td>
<td style="width: 17.5097%; text-align: center;">x64</td>
<td style="width: 13.6799%;">DLL</td>
<td style="width: 19.8675%; text-align: center;">13</td>
<td style="width: 89.4252%;">Fake <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">MpClient.dll</span> sideload</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 10.6367%; text-align: center;">C</td>
<td style="width: 17.5097%; text-align: center;">x86</td>
<td style="width: 13.6799%;">EXE</td>
<td style="width: 19.8675%; text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="width: 89.4252%;">Go loader 32-bit (shared with Lumma Stealer campaign)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 10.6367%; text-align: center;">D</td>
<td style="width: 17.5097%; text-align: center;">x64</td>
<td style="width: 13.6799%;">EXE</td>
<td style="width: 19.8675%; text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="width: 89.4252%;">Vidar core payload</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><span style="font-size: 10pt;">Table 1. Sample clusters with filetype.</span></p>
<p>Cluster B DLL variants export Windows Defender <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">MpClient.dll</span> API functions to enable DLL search-order hijacking (<a href="https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/001/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">MITRE ATT&amp;CK® T1574.002</a>). When a legitimate Windows Defender binary attempts to load <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">MpClient.dll</span>, the operating system locates the malicious copy first if it is placed in a higher-priority search path. The exported function names mimicked include <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">MpAllocMemory, MpClientUtilExportFunctions, MpConfigOpen, MpFreeMemory</span> and nine others.</p>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_3ao7n0j5ztyy"></a>File-Size Inflation</h2>
<p>Loaders in Clusters A and C append hundreds of megabytes of null bytes after the last PE section, pushing the total file size to as high as 491 MB. Most automated sandbox environments enforce an upper file-size limit of 50-100 MB and silently skip oversized submissions, meaning the malware never executes in the analysis environment.</p>
<p>The real malicious content in the largest observed sample is only 2.3 MB, and the remaining 489 MB is null byte padding. Defenders should ensure security tooling removes null byte padding before applying size limits, since the same sample compresses to approximately 2.4 MB.</p>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_y7v80b2ovzf"></a>AMSI Bypass</h2>
<p>Static disassembly of the Vidar core payload sample (SHA256 hash: <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">7ed4a256e1d281cb4f194d13ff554fb280dafde0a67a18115ea038ea6c87d</span>) reveals an in-memory Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) bypass that executes before any stealer logic runs. The routine loads <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">amsi.dll</span>, resolves the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">AmsiScanBuffer</span> variable and overwrites its first six bytes with a patch. This patch forces the function to return <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">E_INVALIDARG</span>, which might disable Windows AMSI for all subsequent script and code execution on the victim machine.</p>
<p>Both the DLL name and function name are <a href="https://www.sans.org/blog/tools-for-examining-xor-obfuscation-for-malware-analysis" target="_blank" rel="noopener">XOR-obfuscated</a> with single-byte key <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">0x05</span> to evade static string scanning. Table 2 shows the encoded and decoded strings for these names.</p>
<table style="width: 98.2667%;">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="width: 37.9603%; text-align: center;"><strong>Encoded String</strong></td>
<td style="width: 22.0963%; text-align: center;"><strong>XOR Key</strong></td>
<td style="width: 301.133%; text-align: center;"><strong>Decoded String</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 37.9603%;"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">dhvl+aii</span></td>
<td style="width: 22.0963%; text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: georgia, palatino, serif;">0x05</span></td>
<td style="width: 301.133%;"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">amsi.dll</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 37.9603%;"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">DhvlVfdkGpcc\&#96;w</span></td>
<td style="width: 22.0963%; text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: georgia, palatino, serif;">0x05</span></td>
<td style="width: 301.133%;"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">AmsiScanBuffer</span></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><span style="font-size: 10pt;">Table 2. Encoded and decoded strings from the sample.</span></p>
<p>Figure 4 below shows patched bytes written to the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">AmsiScanBuffer</span> location (<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">0x80070057</span>).</p>
<figure id="attachment_183321" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-183321" style="width: 703px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-183321 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-679409-183287-4.png" alt="A screenshot of a code snippet showing assembly instructions. It includes a move operation to the EAX register with a value, followed by a return operation." width="703" height="69" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-183321" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 4. AMSI buffer bytes.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The binary uses a second, longer obfuscation layer for larger data blobs. This layer is obfuscated by a 32-byte rotating XOR with the key <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">69946018ddda1058ce5c2a556c78a747838865c47074dcb165effb0840cb1cf5</span> applied to the Telegram bot token, Monero wallet address and mining pool hostname for the XMRig payload.</p>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_dks3104dj7im"></a>Attack Chain</h2>
<p>Figure 5 shows that the attack chain begins with malvertising, luring victims into downloading a password-protected <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">.bin</span> archive disguised as a cracked version of a legitimate program.</p>
<figure id="attachment_183332" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-183332" style="width: 884px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-183332 size-large lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-681255-183287-5-884x700.png" alt="A flowchart diagram illustrating the cyberattack path. At the top, it starts with a &quot;Fake Crack Download,&quot; labeled as generic, leading to the &quot;Factory-V3 Go Loader,&quot; signed with a fake justwatch.com certificate. From the loader, the payload drops include &quot;Vidar + XMRig + Persistence.&quot; Arrows point to three processes: &quot;Vidar Stealer&quot; (stealing credentials and wallets), &quot;XMRig Miner&quot; (mining Monero), and &quot;C2 Notification&quot; (Telegram message labeled as &quot;X3D Miner 'New Log'&quot;)." width="884" height="700" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-681255-183287-5-884x700.png 884w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-681255-183287-5-555x440.png 555w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-681255-183287-5-768x608.png 768w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/word-image-681255-183287-5.png 1472w" sizes="(max-width: 884px) 100vw, 884px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-183332" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 5. Execution chain X3D MINER/Vidar Stealer via Factory-v3.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The loader extracted from the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">.bin</span> archive exhibits the following features:</p>
<ul>
<li>It leverages the Factory-v3 Go framework</li>
<li>It is signed with a fake JustWatch certificate</li>
<li>It is padded with null bytes to reach a large file size of hundreds of MB to evade detection</li>
</ul>
<p>The malware employs anti-analysis techniques such as process enumeration, alongside an AMSI bypass where the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">AmsiScanBuffer</span> function is patched to prevent detection by some types of security software.</p>
<p>Subsequently, the malware drops multiple payloads including Vidar stealer and the XMRig cryptocurrency miner, while establishing persistence mechanisms through registry modifications and scheduled tasks.</p>
<p>The next stage involves reconnaissance, as the malware gathers information about files, hardware IDs (HWID) and bypasses proxies. Vidar stealer then exfiltrates sensitive data such as credentials and cryptocurrency wallets, communicating with a command-and-control (C2) server at <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">136.243.203[.]109</span>.</p>
<p>Simultaneously, XMRig begins mining Monero using the mining pool at <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pool.supportxmr[.]com</span>. Finally, the attacker is notified of new activity via Telegram, with messages labeled "<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">X3D MINER • NEW LOG</span>," ensuring the operator stays informed about successful infections and stolen data. This means the threat actor behind Vidar is deploying the X3D MINER XMRig package.</p>
<p>Dynamic analysis of the Vidar core payload confirmed the following execution sequence:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Geolocation beacon</strong>: GET request to <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">ip-api[.]com/json</span> resolves the victim's public IP address and country, which are embedded in the subsequent Telegram alert</li>
<li><strong>Payload drop</strong>: It drops <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">MicrosoftUpdate.exe</span> in the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">%TEMP%</span> directory as part of the Vidar stealer component and it places the following files in <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">%AppData%\Temp%AppData%\Temp</span>
<ol>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe</span> (the XMRig launcher)</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">libuv-1.dll</span> (an XMRig dependency)</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">WinRing0x64.sys</span> (an XMRig kernel driver)</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">mgwthmc2.dat</span> (an XMRig Monero configuration file)</li>
<li>It copies itself to this folder as <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">NisSrv.exe</span> for persistence</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li><strong>Vidar stealer</strong>: <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">MicrosoftUpdate.exe</span> is written to <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">%TEMP%</span> and executed. It targets browser credential stores, cookies and crypto wallet data, packaging everything into a ZIP for exfiltration to <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">136.243.203[.]109:443</span>.</li>
<li><strong>XMRig miner</strong>: <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe</span> is launched with <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">--config=mgwthmc2.dat</span>. The configuration is built entirely in memory before being written to disk, with the Monero wallet address and pool details decrypted from encrypted blobs. Each victim's <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">C:\</span> volume serial number is hashed into an 8-character HWID that is appended to the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">auth_token</span> field, allowing the operator to track per-victim mining output in the Monero pool dashboard.</li>
</ol>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_v52frr472ut3"></a>Persistence Mechanisms</h2>
<p>The payload establishes persistence through three parallel mechanisms:</p>
<p><strong>Registry Run key:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run</span> value name <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">SystemAgentService</span>, data <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">"...\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Temp\NisSrv.exe" -s</span></li>
<li><strong>Scheduled task</strong>:<br />
<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">schtasks /create /tn "SystemAgentService" /tr "NisSrv.exe -s" /sc onlogon /f</span></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Startup folder batch script</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp\FEbJCNWOCKMJ.bat</span></li>
</ul>
<p>All three mechanisms point to the malware file named <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">NisSrv.exe</span>. Attackers chose this filename to blend in with legitimate Windows Defender components, since the real <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">NisSrv.exe</span> is the Network Inspection Service binary.</p>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_gfjkgzie189n"></a>X3D MINER</h2>
<p>The tag X3D MINER appears in Telegram operator notifications sent for every new victim infection. This moniker is used by a group associated with <a href="https://teletype.in/@x3dminer/kWnLYHhXa8X" target="_blank" rel="noopener">XMRig and binding XMRig with other programs</a>.</p>
<p>The operator behind this campaign runs a dual-monetization scheme. Criminals sell credentials and session cookies stolen by Vidar stealer on criminal log markets, while XMRig provides passive income from hijacked victim CPU cycles. The Factory-v3 builder is assessed to be a separate upstream service used by at least two distinct stealer affiliates.</p>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_ykac54i5uf1x"></a>Variant B</h2>
<p>Pivoting on information from the initial 43 loader samples, we identified 56 additional samples of a subsequent variant on April 24, 2026. This variant retains the same builder, delivery and C2 infrastructure.</p>
<p>The operating characteristics, Go loader, Factory-v3 builder, Telegram dead-drop and payload delivery are identical to the original campaign. The single differentiating factor is the Authenticode certificate. ​​</p>
<p>The operator transitioned from using a self-signed certificate mimicking JustWatch to another unauthorized certificate designed to resemble the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">BleacherReport[.]com certificate</span>. This technique is known as <a href="https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1036/001/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Code Signing Impersonation</a>.</p>
<p>Attackers craft certificates to mimic legitimate, trusted publishers (e.g., Microsoft or Google) by cloning their metadata as Table 3 below shows. It is important to note that Bleacher Report has not been compromised.</p>
<table style="width: 100.148%;">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="width: 14.9068%; text-align: center;"></td>
<td style="width: 30.2904%; text-align: center;"><strong>Variant A</strong></td>
<td style="width: 88.2396%; text-align: center;"><strong>Variant B</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 14.9068%;"><strong>Subject</strong></td>
<td style="width: 30.2904%;"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">CN=justwatch[.]com</span></td>
<td style="width: 88.2396%;"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">CN=\\*.bleacherreport[.]com</span></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 14.9068%;"><strong>Issuer</strong></td>

<td style="width: 88.2396%;"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">CN=GlobalSign Atlas R3 DV TLS CA 2026 Q1 (Cloned issuer name)</span></td>

<p><span style="font-size: 10pt;"><em>Table 3. Certificate data from the old and new variants of Vidar stealer.</em></span></p>
<p>We observed these samples contacting the Telegram channel <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">ci0iiif</span>. New C2 servers in this cluster include <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">138.199.246[.]13, 116.203.243[.]208</span> and <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">136.243.203[.]111</span>.</p>
<h2><a id="post-183287-_2an8ryq91inv"></a>Conclusion</h2>
<p>This campaign demonstrated a multi-layer evasion approach. This approach combined the following characteristics:</p>
<ul>
<li>Rogue certificates</li>
<li>Go-compiled loaders with per-build unique hashes</li>
<li>Binaries inflated to hundreds of MB with null byte padding</li>
<li>An in-memory AMSI bypass</li>
</ul>
<p>Loader samples sharing these characteristics were all delivered via a MaaS platform that also serves other malware stealer families.</p>
<p>The operator's shift from using a self-signed certificate to leveraging an unauthorized certificate in Variant B demonstrates the actor's ability to adapt rapidly.</p>
<p>We recommend that organizations enforce strong Authenticode chain validation and supplement it with:</p>
<ul>
<li>Certificate serial blocklisting</li>
<li>Configuring security tooling to scan files regardless of size</li>
<li>Monitoring for <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">MpClient.dll</span> loading from non-standard paths.</li>
</ul>
<p>Defenders should also:</p>
<ul>
<li>Hunt for the persistence indicators and file-drop patterns described above</li>
<li>Block outbound connections to all C2 addresses and <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">pool.supportxmr[.]com</span> immediately</li>
</ul>

<h3><a id="post-183287-_4olshbpqvpix"></a>Import Hash (imphash) Analysis</h3>
<p>Table 4 shows the imphashes with the associated sample clusters and the role of those clusters in this activity.</p>
<table style="width: 99.1054%;">
<tbody>

	$(subscription_form).submit(function(e) {
		e.preventDefault();
		e.stopImmediatePropagation();
		updateEmailMask();
		var success = true;
		var form = $(this);
		var mail = form.find('input[name="Email"]');
		
		if (mail.val() === '') {
			mail.addClass('has-error');
			showError(1);
			success = false;	
		}  else if (!isEmail(mail.val())){
			showError(2);
			success = false;
		}
		else {
			mail.removeClass('has-error');
			$('.error-mail').addClass('d-none');
		}

		

		if (success) {
                                                if(grecaptcha){
                        grecaptcha.enterprise.ready(function() {
                            grecaptcha.enterprise.execute(SITE_KEY, {action: 'submit'}).then(function(token) {
                                submitSubscribeForm({token :token, action : 'submit'},form);
                            });
                        });
                    }
                    			
		}
		return false;
	});
        function submitSubscribeForm(tokenData, form){
            var serialized_data = form.serialize();
            let captchaParams = `&g-recaptcha-response=${tokenData.token}&action=${tokenData.action}`;
            $.ajax({
				type: 'POST',
				url: form.attr('action'),
				data: serialized_data+captchaParams,
				beforeSend: function() {
                 form.find('button').addClass('is-loading');
    			},
				success: function(msg) {
					form.find('.form-success-message').html('<p class="success-message">You have been successfully subscribed</p>');
					form.find('button').removeClass('is-loading');
					$(email).val('');
					clearError();
				},
				error: function(jqXHR, textStatus, errorThrown) {
					$(subscription_form_button).addClass('is-disabled', true);
					form.find('button').removeClass('is-loading');
					
				}
			});
            
        }
	function showError(error_type){
		if(error_type == 1) {
			$('.error-mail').text("Please enter the email address.").addClass('error-show');
			$(subscription_form_button).addClass('is-disabled');
		} else if(error_type == 2){
			$('.error-mail').text("Please provide a valid e-mail address.").addClass('error-show');
			$(subscription_form_button).addClass('is-disabled');
		}	
		$(subscription_form_button).removeClass('is-loading');
	}
	function clearError(){
		$('.error-mail').text("").removeClass('error-show');;
		$(subscription_form_button).removeClass('is-loading');
		$(subscription_form_button).removeClass('is-disabled');
	}
	
	$(email).on('input', function (event) { 
		var email = $(this).val();
		if (isEmail(email) ) {			
			clearError();
		} else if(email == ""){
			clearError();
		} else{
			showError(2);			  
		}
    });

	function isEmail(email) {
		var re = /^(([^<>()\[\]\\.,;:\s@"]+(\.[^<>()\[\]\\.,;:\s@"]+)*)|(".+"))@((\[[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\])|(([a-zA-Z\-0-9]+\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}))$/;
		return re.test(String(email).toLowerCase());
	}
	
	
	
	function updateEmailMask() {
		var email = $("#unit42footerSubscription_form input[name='Email']").val();
		if (email && email.trim() != '') {
			var maskedEmail = maskEmailAddress(email);
			$("#unit42footerSubscription_form input[name='emailFormMask']").val(maskedEmail);
		}
	}

	function maskEmailAddress (emailAddress) {
		function mask(str) {
			var strLen = str.length;
			if (strLen > 4) {
				return str.substr(0, 1) + str.substr(1, strLen - 1).replace(/\w/g, '*') + str.substr(-1,1);
			}
			return str.replace(/\w/g, '*');
		}
		return emailAddress.replace(/([\w.]+)@([\w.]+)(\.[\w.]+)/g, function (m, p1, p2, p3) {
			return mask(p1) + '@' + mask(p2) + p3;
		});

		return emailAddress;
	}

}(jQuery));
//# sourceMappingURL=main.js.map
	
</script>
<!--  End: Footer subscription form -->

	$(document).ready(function(){
		$("html").on("click", ".language-btn", function () {
			$(this).toggleClass("expand");
			$(".language-dropdown").toggleClass("expand");

				$(".language-dropdown").removeClass("expand");
			}
		});
	});

	var isProcessing = false; 
    function alter_ul_post_values(obj,post_id,ul_type){
	
		if (isProcessing)    
		return;  
		isProcessing = true;   
		var like_nonce = jQuery('#_wpnonce').val();
		jQuery(obj).find("span").html("..");
                jQuery.ajax({
                    type: "POST",
                    url: "https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/plugins/like-dislike-counter-for-posts-pages-and-comments/ajax_counter.php",
                    data: "post_id="+post_id+"&up_type="+ul_type+"&ul_nonce="+like_nonce,
                    success: function(msg){
                            jQuery(obj).find("span").html(msg);
                            isProcessing = false; 
                            jQuery(obj).find('svg').children('path').attr('stroke','#0050FF');
                            jQuery(obj).removeClass('idc_ul_cont_not_liked idc_ul_cont_not_liked_inner');
                    }
 		});
	}

    event.preventDefault();

       OneTrust.ToggleInfoDisplay();
    }else{
      var href = event.target.getAttribute('href');

}

function loadScript(url, defer){
    var script1 = document.createElement('script');
    script1.setAttribute('type', 'text/javascript');
    script1.setAttribute('src',url);
    if(defer == true){
        script1.setAttribute('defer','defer');
    }
    document.head.appendChild(script1);
}
function loadScript1(url, callback){

    var script = document.createElement("script")
    script.type = "text/javascript";
    if (script.readyState){  //IE
        script.onreadystatechange = function(){
            if (script.readyState == "loaded" || script.readyState == "complete"){
                script.onreadystatechange = null;
                callback();
            }
        };
    } else {  //Others
        script.onload = function(){
            callback();
        };
    }
    script.src = url;
    document.getElementsByTagName("head")[0].appendChild(script);
}
if(referer == "CloudCortex" || referer == "Prisma" || referer == "Cortex" || referer == "Sase" || referer == "Unit" || referer == "Ngfw" || referer == "Idira"){

    setTimeout(function(){
      loadScript(main_site_criticalTopBase, false);
      loadScript1(main_site_criticalTopProductNav, function(){
        window.PAN_initializeProduct2021Nav();
      });
      loadScript(main_site_defered, false);
    }, 3000);
	}
	else{
    setTimeout(function(){
      loadScript1(main_site_critical_top, function(){
        window.PAN_initializeProduct2021Nav();
      });
      loadScript(main_site_defered, false);
    }, 3000);
	}
}

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function() {
  // Find all the forms on the page
  var forms = document.getElementsByTagName("form");

  // Loop through each form
  for (var i = 0; i < forms.length; i++) {
    var form = forms[i];

    // Check if the hidden input field already exists
    var requestInput = form.querySelector("input[name='web_unit42_req_id']");
    if (!requestInput) {
      // Create a hidden input element if it doesn't exist
      requestInput = document.createElement("input");
      requestInput.type = "hidden";
      requestInput.name = "web_unit42_req_id";
      requestInput.id = "web_unit42_req_id";

      // Append the hidden field to the form
      form.appendChild(requestInput);
    }
  }
});

// Assign the onCheqResponse function to the window object to handle events from any form
window.onCheqResponse = function(encryptedMessage, requestID) {
  // Find all the forms on the page
  var forms = document.getElementsByTagName("form");

  for (var i = 0; i < forms.length; i++) {
    var form = forms[i];
    var requestInput = form.querySelector("input[name='web_unit42_req_id']");
    if (requestInput) {
      requestInput.value = requestID;
    }
  }
};
